text: "I See You" is the eighth episode of the third season of Breaking Bad and the 28th episode overall. Written by Gennifer Hutchison and directed by Colin Bucksey, it originally aired on AMC in the United States and Canada on May 9, 2010. The episode's title is a play on "ICU," referencing the intensive care unit of a hospital. As Jesse Pinkman leaves the hospital after Hank Schrader's attack, he sees Hank being admitted in critical condition with four gunshot wounds and smiles to himself, satisfied by the karmic justice, as Skinny Pete picks him up. Walter White tells confused and upset Gale Boetticher that they are not working well together and that he is being replaced; Jesse then arrives, upsetting Walt, and displays his uncouth and unprofessional behavior as he admires the lab, further confusing Gale, who realizes Jesse is his replacement. As Walt leaves, Victor reminds him not to fall behind on their weekly quota. Jesse informs Walt about Hank's condition, prompting Walt to go to the hospital, where Steve Gomez and George Merkert explain that two Cartel hitmen, Leonel and Marco Salamanca, attempted to kill Hank. Gomez is astonished that Hank defeated both without his gun, leading Marie Schrader to question why Hank didn't have his gun, as he had turned it in after being suspended for assaulting Jesse. Marie blames both Gomez and Merkert for not supporting Hank and also blames Walt, believing Hank would never have met Jesse if Walt hadn't "bought marijuana" from him. Leonel, now with amputated legs, is being treated in the same hospital as Hank. When Gomez and Walt visit him from the other side of his door, Leonel recognizes Walt and angrily crawls toward him before being hoisted back to his bed, startling Walt and making him realize he might have been the intended target. Gus Fring receives a call from Juan Bolsa, who suspects Gus orchestrated the hit on a DEA agent, as Marco and Leonel would not have attacked without approval. Bolsa tells Gus he intends to get the truth from Leonel about who authorized the attack. Walt spends the next few days at the hospital while Jesse stays at the lab, waiting for him to return so they can resume cooking to meet their quota. Walt eventually receives a call from Gus to check in; to avoid revealing that his brother-in-law is a DEA agent, Walt lies, claiming Gale has set them back and promises to produce 400 pounds (180 kg) of meth next week, which Gus agrees to. Walt is horrified when Gus suddenly appears at the hospital, bringing free food from Los Pollos Hermanos as a show of support for the DEA. Gus meets Walt's family and shares a memory from when he first met Hank, revealing to Walt that Gus already knew Hank was a DEA agent. In private, Walt assures Gus that Hank is not a problem for their business, and Gus subtly indicates that Leonel will no longer be a threat. As he leaves, Leonel suddenly goes into cardiac arrest and dies. Mike Ehrmantraut is then shown disposing of a syringe and leaving unnoticed, with Gus's appearance serving as a distraction for Mike's actions, and Gomez celebrates. Later that night, Gus receives another call from Bolsa, whose house is now surrounded by Mexican federales. With Leonel dead, Bolsa believes Gus is responsible and vows retaliation, but is interrupted by the federales. His bodyguards are shot and killed, and as Bolsa attempts to escape, he is shot to death. The episode was written by Gennifer Hutchison and directed by Colin Bucksey, and aired on AMC in the United States and Canada on May 9, 2010. Donna Bowman of The A.V. Club noted that the episode focuses on the organization employing Walter, highlighting its long reach and ruthless ambition, but criticized the hospital scene as "spouting clichés." Seth Amitin of IGN gave the episode a 9.4/10 rating, calling it "a great episode about the emotional debris left in the wake of last week's amazing melee." In 2019, The Ringer ranked "I See You" 47th out of the 62 total Breaking Bad episodes, and Vulture ranked it 61st overall. The episode's original broadcast was viewed by 1.78 million people, an increase from the 1.52 million who watched the previous episode, "One Minute."
